program.section_heading: Administration of Justice: Corrections - Associate of Science Degree - NAS1097/C
outcomes: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the history and trends of the correctional system in the United States and describe the relationship between corrections and the components of the judicial system.
Analyze and describe the legal issues, specific laws, and general operations of correctional institutions.
Describe the differences between adult, juvenile, probation, and parole corrections systems.
Identify, understand, and demonstrate inmate processing procedures including receiving, discharge, and classification processes.
Assess the legal considerations and the rights of individuals within correctional systems.
Demonstrate professional best practices in methods of professional communications, interviewing and de-escalation techniques.
Identify, understand, and demonstrate appropriate and professional written and oral communication skills.

notes: Under Required Courses the catalog prints 'Select one of the following: 3.00' followed by ADJ-1 and ADJ-1H; read as a choice between the course and its honors twin, recorded as ADJ-1 with ADJ-1H as alternative. The remaining six ADJ courses are read as required, consistent with the stated 21 units (3 + 6 x 3).

Elective Courses: 'Select 9 units from the following' with the line 'Choose from any elective courses in the discipline.' followed by POLS-5 and SOC-20. The electives are not limited to the two listed courses; any course in the discipline (presumably ADJ) may count. Not recorded as open electives because they are discipline-limited, not any course.
No general education pattern is named; the degree text refers only to general education and graduation requirements in the college catalog.
